name: Cold waves & winter storms
summary: No major cold wave or top-tier winter-storm warning confirmed on 12 Nov; polar vortex disruption raises later cold risk
state: Searches on 12 Nov found no confirmed top-tier cold or winter-storm warning across a major region and no cold outbreak causing power or gas outages; the Met Office had no UK weather warnings in force on 12 Nov. The Met Office said on 4 Nov that a weak, short-lived polar vortex reversal could count as a major sudden stratospheric warming, which raises the chance of UK cold from mid-November but is not a forecast of a cold spell. That risk explains the upward trend.
for_you: No widespread cold disruption is under way. Older people and those in poorly heated homes are most exposed if colder weather arrives later in November; the Met Office and UKHSA cold-health alerts give official warnings.
rubric_hit: Normal: no major cold wave or winter storm affecting large populations found as of 12 Nov

why: Severe cold and winter storms kill, cut power and spike gas demand, as in Texas in 2021; they matter most when energy supplies are tight.
drivers: Polar vortex disruption, blocking highs, ENSO, Arctic outbreaks.

rubric.alert: Deadly cold or winter storms with widespread power or gas outages.
rubric.watch: Top-tier cold or winter-storm warnings across a major region, or a cold wave lifting gas demand sharply.
rubric.normal: No major cold wave or winter storm affecting large populations.
